portInfo.description: Seward’s cruise landing is the Dale R. Lindsey Alaska Railroad Intermodal Facility, nicknamed the cruise-ship dock locally. Visit Seward’s cruise guest page states ships moor alongside with no tendering. Alaska Railroad materials describe ownership of docks and adjacent uplands supporting intermodal passenger and freight moves toward Anchorage and Fairbanks. This is a classic southcentral Alaska embarkation/disembarkation gateway for Gulf of Alaska itineraries rather than a Southeast Alaska walk-ashore village call.

thingsToDo.shortCall: Stay near the port area and keep a generous buffer before all-aboard.
thingsToDo.standardCall: Combine a central walk, one attraction, and lunch if times allow—start back well before all-aboard.
thingsToDo.longerCall: A second stop or coach outing is realistic only with confirmed transport and an eight-hour or longer window.
thingsToDo.practicalTip: No tender — but still budget time for rail/bus connections if continuing to Anchorage the same day.
